content.text:
I added a target-user check to `getCredentialOfferState` in `OID4VCAuthorizationDetailsProcessor.java`, so User B can no longer present an offer targeted to User A. I haven't compiled it or run any tests.

The existing check there only compared the offer's target client. `buildAuthorizationDetailResponse` and `handleMissingAuthorizationDetails` both call this method, and it runs when the token is issued, before `afterAuthorizationDetailsProcessed` creates the issued-credential record. So a stolen offer is now rejected before any record exists for User B, and the refresh path never gets a chance to null the `credentialsOfferId` link. When an offer has a non-null `targetUserId` that differs from the logged-in user, it throws `IllegalStateException`, the same way the existing client-mismatch check does.

The pre-authorized code flow is unaffected, because its session user is already the offer's target. I left the Credential Endpoint's own check as it was.

The graph index was rebuilding during this task, so my queries were slow.
